rules: Shape is mandatory geometry and each Index Polygon must be a single area.
Poly_ID is a mandatory numeric unique polygon reference managed through dataset lifecycle rules.
Title_No is a mandatory character identifier for the registered title.
INSERT is the mandatory date when the polygon was initially created on the index map.
UPDATE is the mandatory date when all or part of the title was last updated.
Vers_No is the mandatory numeric version of Poly_ID.
Rec_Status is a mandatory character field describing polygon record status.
Rec_Status values are Added A, Changed C or Deleted D.
Indicative Extent current practice is the most common feature and is a good representation of the title plan.
Footprint current practice supports index-map interpretation where multiple titles occur in one building.
The National Polygon Dataset is published and updated monthly.
Blank CSV fields are sent with no character between enclosing double quotes.
National Polygon delivery dates use DD-MM-YYYY format.
Line separation is removed from delivered National Polygon CSV data.
The first CSV row contains column heading names.
National Polygon change-only files follow LR_POLY_COU_<DD_MMM_YYYY>.

The 1m composite DTM is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters.
The raster delivery is divided into 5km tiles.
The 5km raster tiles are aligned to the OS National Grid.
The DTM values are presented in metres.
The DTM is vertically referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The published dataset uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
The official metadata states there are no public-access constraints.
The dataset is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The metadata records an annual update frequency.
The metadata carries Environment Agency copyright and database-right attribution for 2022.
The official geographic latitude extent is 49.943 to 55.816.
The official geographic longitude extent is -6.236 to 2.072.
The LIDAR Tiles Catalogues FeatureServer exposes DTM and DSM time-stamped extent layers as layer IDs 0 and 1.
The FeatureServer supports JSON queries with a maximum record count of 1000.

OS Terrain 50 contour GML is feature-based with ContourLine, SpotHeight and LandWaterBoundary feature types.
ContourLine uses GM_LineString geometry and master, ordinary or auxiliary type values; master and ordinary correspond to index and standard contours.
ContourLine propertyValue is a Distance representing contour length.
SpotHeight propertyValue is the z height above Newlyn or another British height datum.
SpotHeightType supports formSpot, generic, mountainPass and summit values.
The current product uses the generic SpotHeight subtype.
LandWaterBoundary propertyValue is a Distance representing boundary-line length.
Water-level categories distinguish mean high/low water in England and Wales from mean high/low water springs in Scotland.
Feature identifiers follow os.t50.<tile name>.<sequential number>.
Geometry identifiers use the feature identifier with a .geom suffix.
Every feature and geometry identifier is guaranteed unique within a product release.
OS Terrain products are updated by whole-tile refresh and do not provide feature-based change-only updates.
Sequential identifiers are regenerated when a tile is updated.
Terrain 50 GML geometry CRS is expressed as urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700.
The contour model uses propertyValue and the shapefile representation abbreviates it to PROP_VALUE because of the ten-character field limit.
No contours are supplied between mean high and mean low water lines.
Tile-average tidal heights can create a small discrete step between adjacent tiles.
Interpolated spot heights cannot be guaranteed to be summits or the highest points of features.
